interface.title: Exoplanet Radius Explorer
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis of a public catalogue (sample selection, visual comparison, simple statistics, export)
interface.what_it_is_for: Load the NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars composite table, filter it by discovery method, stellar-age group, radius, period, distance and quality cuts, then compare stellar age and orbital period against planet radius using rank correlations, a host-star bootstrap of the young-to-old radius ratio, and a period-detrended radius-valley histogram.

data.note: This repository commit has no src/ or data/ directory. The setup agent wrote stand-in src/config, data, transform, science and plots modules, plus the demo CSV, from app.py's imports (plan.json data.why). All counts, statistics and rendering below therefore come from the author's app.py running on stand-in code and data, not from the author's full tool. With the network unavailable, the app falls back to a seeded synthetic table (42 rows; red 'Synthetic data' banner: screens/004.webp, screens/049.webp). I turned off 'Query the archive over the network' and uploaded sample_pscomppars_export.csv. The app reported 'Loaded sample_pscomppars_export.csv (20 rows)', with 17 planets left after cleaning (screens/007.webp). Later I reloaded the page to get the larger synthetic table back for the valley and bootstrap tests (screens/049.webp onward).
harness_artefacts: Bootstrap hang: whenever the '< 100 Myr' group was selected (upload or synthetic, with or without Imaging), the young-to-old table stayed at 'Bootstrapping the median ratio…' and never finished, which also kept the later tabs from rendering (screens/011.webp, 017.webp, 026.webp, 052.webp, 054.webp; check/screens/045.webp). The review attributes this to the stand-in science code.

Reference radii drawn at 10^R: with 'Reference radii' on (the default), the radius axis stretches to about 10^10 and the lines sit at roughly 10^R (Earth ~10, Neptune ~10^4, Jupiter ~10^10), squashing the data. The stand-in seed/src/plots.py:70 calls add_hline on a log axis, so Plotly reads y=3.88 as 10^3.88. Turning the overlay off gives a readable plot (screens/028.webp vs 029.webp; check/screens/012.webp, check/screens/016.webp).
Empty Density view: switching the period plot to Density drew an empty heatmap (count scale ±0.5) with no points (screens/036.webp), produced by the stand-in plotting code.
